statements.t: Additionally, we aim to refresh our product offerings continuously to align with evolving market trends.
We aim to design an app that will bring users a comprehensive intelligent experience to create a safer and more satisfying riding life.

We intend to continue investing in future feature enhancements and iterative releases to support the platform’s long-term evolution, subject to our ongoing assessment of business needs and resource allocation.
The Company disputes the allegations in the complaint and intends to defend the case vigorously.

On October 27, 2026, the Court granted the Company’s request to fully brief a motion to dismiss the Second Amended Complaint; that motion will be fully briefed and submitted for the Court’s consideration in January 2027, and the Company expects a decision at some point in mid-2027.
On September 15, 2025, the Company planned to hold a special meeting of stockholders, but adjourned to October 13, 2025 in order to achieve a quorum (the “Special Meeting”).

The divestitures were not intended to be a strategic withdrawal from any specific geographic region or industry, but rather to streamline the Company’s corporate structure and reduce complexity in financial reporting.

Our growth will depend on our ability to achieve sales targets, including our ability to attract new customers, which in turn depends in part on our ability to execute our retail strategy and produce effective marketing initiatives to expand our brand perception with prospective customers.

With respect to branding and marketing, we plan to raise brand awareness through both traditional and social media channels and connect with customers through physical touchpoints such as our retail stores and distributors.
In addition, we intend to provide superior customer experience through our trained technicians who will provide after-sale maintenance and repair services at our retail stores.
We expect our store count to remain stable in the near term and do not anticipate any significant fluctuations in payroll expenses in the next quarter.
Each of our retail stores has a minimum of two employees, and additional office employees will be hired to support retail stores in customer service and marketing.
However, increased competition may pressure prices and margins, reducing sales volume, revenues, and sales margin for us.
We also benefit from environmental regulations in our target markets which include economic incentives to purchasers of EVs and tax credits for EV manufacturers.

We expect that, in the foreseeable future, selling and marketing expenses will remain generally stable, primarily due to the fact that our retail store count has been streamlined and is not expected to undergo further changes; however, should we further expand our market presence, such expenses may rise accordingly.

We expect that, in the foreseeable future, general and administrative expenses will remain generally stable, primarily as a result of our streamlined retail store count, which is not expected to undergo further changes; however, should we further expand our market presence in the future, general and administrative activities may increase, and such expenses will rise accordingly.

The net decrease was primarily due to reductions in payroll expenses, rent expenses, insurance expenses, depreciation expenses, and other related expenses resulting from the reduction in our retail store count and the downsizing of our business operations, partially offset by increases in expected credit loss expense and professional fees.

The net decrease in operating expenses was primarily attributable to reductions in payroll expenses, rent expenses, insurance expenses, depreciation expenses, and professional fees as a result of the reduction in retail stores and the downsizing of our business operations, partially offset by (i) an increase in expected credit losses, and (ii) increased development fees incurred in connection with iterative…

Management has considered the historical experience, the economy, trends in the retail industry, the expected collectability of the accounts receivable and the realization of the inventories as of September 30, 2026.

The Company is in ongoing negotiations with the bank for a renewal or further extension; however, there can be no assurance that such negotiations will be successful or that the bank will not exercise its remedies under the loan documents.

For the next 12 months from the issuance date of this report, we plan to alleviate the going concern risk through (i) equity financing to support the Company’s working capital; (ii) other available sources of financing (including debt) from banks and other financial institutions; and (iii) financial support from the Company’s related parties.
We cannot assure you that financing will be available in amounts or on terms acceptable to us, if at all.
As of September 30, 2026 and March 31, 2026, our accounts receivable, net of allowance for expected credit losses, were $9.6 million and $7.0 million, respectively.
Our prepayments and other receivables, net of allowance for expected credit losses, primarily represent prepayments to vendors and other service providers.
We have not been exposed to, nor do we anticipate being exposed to, material risks due to changes in market interest rates.
Our estimated allowance for expected credit losses is based on our assessment of collectability of accounts receivable.
As of September 30, 2026 and March 31, 2026, we recorded allowance for expected credit losses of $1,878,818 and $217,479, respectively.
